messages.content: How did I sleep last night?

content.content: No data: Garmin has no sleep recorded for this date. If the night just ended, the watch may not have synced yet: sync it in the Garmin Connect app and ask again later. Repeating the call right away will not help.

content.text:
**Last night's sleep isn't in Garmin yet.** There's nothing recorded for the night ending this morning (18 March), so your watch probably hasn't synced. Open the Garmin Connect app to sync it, then ask me again and I'll look at it.

The most recent night on record is **Monday night into Tuesday (16–17 March)**:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Sleep score | **63 (Fair)** |
| Time asleep | **5 h 42 min** (about 11:45 pm to 5:40 am) |
| Deep sleep | 1 h 00 min (17.5%) |
| Light sleep | 3 h 32 min (62%) |
| REM sleep | 1 h 10 min (20.5%) |
| Awake | 13 min, woke up twice |
| Overnight HRV | 61 ms |
| Sleep stress (average) | 19, which is low |
| Blood oxygen (SpO2) | 94% on average, lowest 87% |

**What this means:** You didn't get enough sleep, and that's the main reason the score was only Fair. Your sleep quality was fine. The deep and REM sleep percentages were in a normal range, you were awake very little, and your stress level was low overnight. You just didn't sleep long enough.

One more thing: your lowest blood oxygen reading was 87%. Wrist readings often dip like this for a moment, especially if your arm moves, so one low reading isn't a worry. But if it keeps happening and you also snore loudly or wake up tired, mention it to a doctor.

That's the only night recorded in the past week, so I can't compare it with your usual sleep. Wearing the watch to bed more often would make that possible.
